known_allocations.atlas_layer_note: The above breakdown is for measured clearing/heavy scenes, which each have one atlas layer. Material Atelier allocation is from its O01 report and has a smaller geometry buffer.

clearing_or_heavy.notes: Vertex input is seven shadow draws plus opaque draw. These are logical attachment and vertex references, not physical DRAM traffic. Tile memory, caches, compression and overdraw change external traffic. Shader texture reads are variable and excluded. Effect target uses Rg16Float here, reducing modeled full-frame effect-target clear/write traffic by 921600 bytes versus the original Rgba16Float estimate; this remains logical traffic, not measured DRAM bandwidth.

optical_frame_additions.notes: One HDR snapshot is allocated on first camera-visible optical batch and copied on each frame with a camera-visible optical batch. The original normal/depth target is sampled read-only and is no longer copied or attached for optical output. This removes 7,372,800 modeled logical copy/attachment bytes per active optical frame versus the prior two-snapshot/two-attachment path; estimates are not physical DRAM traffic.

smoke_compute_per_fixed_step.notes: Nominal source footprint counts two eight-texel filtered samples and one RGBA16F store. The shader uses x/y channels from samples; filtering hardware, channel elimination, caching and implementation details mean this is neither measured bus bandwidth nor guaranteed physical bytes. Current implementation uses two-channel Rg16Float ping-pong volumes; nominal full-texel request arithmetic is halved from the original RGBA16F inventory. This is not measured external-memory traffic.

uploads.notes: The fire frame is cached by its fixed-tick key; without a changed tick, camera-only render refreshes globals/matrices but not FireFrame. Upload payload excludes queue staging/alignment.

evidence_and_candidates.interpretation: Existing route data shows smoke compute well below render stages on this M1 Max/Metal build; active-region simulation is not justified by the current timing. Stage timestamps overlap and route values describe complete variants.

evidence_and_candidates.not_recommended_from_current_evidence: Active-region smoke simulation: current measured compute is about 0.0205 ms median while post and atmosphere/fire are multi-millisecond stages.

limitations_and_open_gates: No hardware DRAM/bandwidth counters were collected; attachment, copy and filtered-sample byte totals are logical operation estimates.
The only live format capability probe is Apple M1 Max/Metal. Windows DX12 and RTX-class feature reports and measured pass costs remain open.
RG16 capability in this probe does not make it a portable default; query each adapter and retain an RGBA16F fallback unless DX12 and target GPU results pass.
Repeat the inventory after O03/O05/O06 introduce or specialize targets, as required by the plan.
One HDR snapshot and its copy remain necessary in the current pass layout; eliminating it requires a larger sampling/output redesign and matched backend timing.

The opt-in Rg11b10Ufloat HDR target was tested only on Apple M1 Max/Metal; baseline/fallback rendering, Windows DX12 and other adapters remain required. Three fixed-tick still views show low mean channel error but are not temporal or performance acceptance.

compact_hdr_rg11b10.status: implemented as an opt-in startup format; Rgba16Float remains the default and fallback
compact_hdr_rg11b10.visual_review: The matched metal, smoke and glass stills were inspected at native capture scale and look very similar; output pixels are not byte-identical, and smoke has a 30/255 maximum single-channel difference in sparse pixels.

optical_normal_snapshot_removal.interpretation: No meaningful timing gain established. Optical-resolve paired GPU deltas were mixed and had a -0.004874 ms median; total GPU render median delta was -0.011916 ms, while frame-work deltas were mixed (-0.042875, -0.047626, +0.108209 ms). Three route pairs are insufficient to claim a performance improvement. Memory and logical-traffic reductions are reported separately and are not measured bandwidth.
optical_normal_snapshot_removal.limits: One Apple M1 Max/Metal adapter; short 20-second serial route pairs, no DX12/RTX or native-window results.

optical_normal_snapshot_removal_60s.interpretation: No GPU timing benefit measured on this route. Whole-GPU paired deltas were +0.000293, -0.008875, +0.024748 ms (median +0.000293 ms); optical-resolve deltas were +0.008666, -0.012167, +0.034459 ms (median +0.008666 ms). Frame-work deltas were all negative but varied substantially (-0.009832, -0.133666, -0.406791 ms), so do not attribute them to the GPU pass change. Keep the result as memory/logical traffic savings only.
optical_normal_snapshot_removal_60s.limits: One Apple M1 Max/Metal adapter; three 60-second serial material-orbit pairs with 10-second warmup, no Windows DX12/RTX or native-window results.

known_allocation_bytes.note: descriptor/structure estimate; excludes driver alignment and transient/pipeline/query storage

temporal_fixed_camera_capture_review.visual_review: Matched rows looked visually alike through fire/smoke temporal changes; no new visible instability identified at the sampled ticks. Captures keep a fixed hero camera, so they do not visually replay the moving material-orbit camera route.

compact_hdr_route_validation.interpretation: On this M1 Max/Metal adapter, candidate GPU-render medians were consistently 0.0051–0.0092 ms lower (median paired delta -0.006125 ms, about 0.24% of baseline). Frame-work deltas varied (-0.1287, +0.0143, -0.0644 ms; median -0.0644 ms). The small GPU difference is not sufficient to establish a practical performance gain; treat the established benefit as 1,843,200 bytes lower known target allocation at 640x360, with reduced channel precision and visible quantization differences. Keep opt-in.
compact_hdr_route_validation.limits: One Apple M1 Max/Metal adapter; 3 alternating paired 120s serial offscreen runs after 10s warmup. No native-window pacing, Windows DX12/RTX or fallback-adapter exercise. Temporal image review sampled four fixed ticks at a fixed camera and does not replace route-camera captures or longer visual review.

compact_hdr_route_camera_review.visual_review: All eight matched baseline/candidate poses looked alike in the contact sheet, with no distinct route-dependent artifact identified. Most pixels have small quantization changes; numerical details vary with viewpoint. Same fixed simulation tick at every camera pose isolates route viewpoint and does not show simultaneous route-time fire/smoke evolution.
compact_hdr_route_camera_review.limits: Single Apple M1 Max/Metal adapter; fixed tick and seed; eight sampled poses at 15-second intervals rather than continuous capture; no fallback adapter or DX12 validation.

optical_no_copy_experiment.hypothesis: Replace the per-frame HDR snapshot copy with a separate optical color overlay and R8Unorm coverage mask, preserving the immutable HDR source for reflection/refraction reads.
optical_no_copy_experiment.implementation: Opt-in render.optical_no_copy / engine-lab --optical-no-copy. Clears a lazily allocated optical overlay and mask on visible optical frames, renders optical results there, then post selects covered pixels. Default path remains snapshot-copy. Unsupported R8Unorm render/sample capability falls back to snapshot-copy.

timing.interpretation: GPU render reduction is small (~0.64% of baseline); frame-work deltas vary and no practical end-to-end gain is established. GPU stage intervals may overlap; do not sum stage distributions.

logical_traffic_model.caveat: Full-frame logical access estimate only; not physical DRAM bandwidth and actual shader coverage/cache/tile behavior varies.
